messages:
Nina: Noticed a $5.4k reclassification risk on last invoice. A bunch of GPU hours billed to `customer-poc` projects look like internal experiments. We should reconcile before we submit an invoice dispute to the cloud vendor.

cost-bot: ALERT: Label mismatch detected across billing export vs inventory (2024-11-02). Potential customer->internal reclassification = $5,400. Details: /alerts/1678

Omar: I pulled the raw export. The tricky part: some projects have `customer=poc-acme` in resource metadata but the actual usage came from VMs provisioned by CI for nightly experiments (owner: infra-ci-service). So we have conflicting owner vs customer tags.

Priya: If we misclassify and then contest the invoice, vendor will ask for evidence linking compute to customer contracts. We need an audit trail before any dispute.

Ravi: Agreed. Suggest process: (1) run a usage-level join between billing.export and internal inventory to map instance_id -> provisioner, (2) surface ambiguous instances where provisioner != customer owner, (3) route ambiguous items to team owners for confirmation.

Omar: SQL I ran to find ambiguous instances:

```sql
SELECT be.instance_id, be.project_id, be.cost, inv.provisioner, inv.customer_tag
FROM `billing.export` be
LEFT JOIN `inventory.instances` inv ON be.instance_id = inv.id
WHERE be.usage_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 14 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
  AND inv.customer_tag IS NOT NULL
  AND inv.provisioner IS NOT NULL
  AND inv.provisioner NOT IN (inv.customer_tag)

ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

Omar: Top rows: instance-1123 (project: customer-poc-acme) cost $2,600 prov: infra-ci-service cust_tag: poc-acme; instance-1189 cost $1,700 prov: playground-operator cust_tag:poc-acme; instance-1302 cost $1,100 prov: model-eval cust_tag:poc-beta

Nina: So ~ $4.3k clearly looks like infra/ci provisioning that got customer tag baked in upstream. That explains the $5.4k variance once you include small items.

Priya: For any items we decide are internal, we should (a) annotate our internal billing view and (b) ask vendor to reclassify on invoice only if >$2k. Below that finance absorbs as internal adjustment to sandbox budget.

Ravi: I'll draft the evidence pack format for vendor disputes: CSV of instance_id, start/end time, provisioner service logs (link), and approval signature from owning team. We should avoid disputing anything where there's no clear owner.

Nina: Also we need to consider committed use discounts (CUDs). If we reassign a chunk of customer-tagged usage to internal, that could affect CUD utilization math and unit price. Ops teams please vet impact before final reclassification.

Omar: Note: there's a 3-day delay in inventory sync — some recent ephemeral instances aren't in inventory yet. We'll exclude usage within last 72h from auto-reclassification and surface them for manual review.

InfraCI: FYI: our provisioning templates will be patched to prevent writing customer= tags when provisioner=infra-ci-service. Will open PR today.

Priya: Approval thresholds proposal: automated suggestion for reclassify when project-level ambiguous cost < $2k OR single instance < $1k. Anything above requires owner sign-off + finance manager (Priya) to approve vendor dispute.

Nina: Action plan: (1) Omar to generate CSV of ambiguous instances and run backfill for last 14 days (due EOD), (2) Ravi to prepare vendor evidence pack template and dispute checklist (2 business days), (3) Ops/Infra to patch templates and update inventory sync (1 day), (4) Priya to confirm approval thresholds and who signs vendor disputes (today).

Omar: Backfill run started. Will post CSV to Ticket FIN-3421 when complete.

cost-bot: NOTE: Dispute candidate job scheduled nightly at 04:00 UTC; excludes usage newer than 72h.

Priya: If final disputed amount > $2k, I'll review and if we escalate I'll need engineering sign-off proving provisioning context. Otherwise finance will absorb.

Ravi: Also recommend we add a dashboard widget: "Potential customer mislabels affecting invoices" with links to instance-level evidence and provisioning service. That will speed triage.

Nina: Good call. Let's keep this thread as the source of truth for FIN-3421. Tag me @Nina when you attach the CSV.

Omar: CSV uploaded to FIN-3421: https://redwood.atlassian.com/FIN-3421/attachment/ambiguous-instances.csv

Nina: Thanks. We'll hold off on vendor dispute until we collect owner confirmations. If we don't get replies in 72h, default to internal charge and log for later reconciliation. :memo:
